text:
incident-bot: PAGE: High error rate from serving-runtime pool 'tp-prod' — multiple CUDA OOMs and communicator timeouts. Paging on-call.

alice: I'm on it — seeing alert spikes from two clusters in us-west-2 and eu-central.

ben: confirming logs show repeated 'NCCL WARN Timeout' and then `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in the same container PID.

carla: how widespread? single model or many?

alice: looks like one model variant (gpt-13k-quant) serving tensor-parallel shards; roughly 12 nodes showing errors, ~40% of requests failing for this route.

dan: customer impact: internal canary shows SLO breach and at least 3 paying customers have 502 spikes, support ticket #9802 opened.

ella: escalation: move traffic off this model variant to fallback (gpt-13k-vanilla) and enable degraded latency SLO. Any objections?

frank: agree. I'm spinning up fallback pool now. Command I'm running: `rctl reroute --route /v1/generate --from model:gpt-13k-quant --to model:gpt-13k-vanilla --weight 100`

carla: nice. also let's reduce batch size and disable auto-batching for the offending route while we investigate.

ben: adding flags to runtime config: `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1`, `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` to mitigate fragmentation. Applying to the k8s daemonset.

alice: log excerpt from one node: ```
[2026-03-15 03:21:07] runtime: ncclCommInitRank: NCCL WARN Call to cuInit failed, error 35
[2026-03-15 03:21:07] runtime: ncclAllReduce failed: NCCL_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION
[2026-03-15 03:21:09] runtime: cudaMemcpy failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15 03:21:10] containerd: oom_kill: process 2431 (python) score 1000
```

gina: support reports customers A and B saw degraded throughput starting 03:20 UTC. ETA on reroute?

frank: reroute complete, traffic now at fallback pool. Confirming dropped error rate in router metrics.

carla: can someone check if KV cache or prefix caching churn caused sudden mem growth?

ben: good call — early traces show a spike in sequence length for a small subset of requests (unbounded system prompts from a partner integration). That likely inflated per-request memory.

dan: ok mitigation plan: 1) block the partner API key temporarily (rate-limit), 2) keep reroute to fallback, 3) roll a targeted restart/drain on affected nodes, 4) capture core dumps and nvml snapshots.

ella: I can handle the API key block — applying a 10 qps limit to that key now.

alice: initiating drain of 6 nodes with repeated OOMs. `kubectl drain node/tp-ux-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then monitor.

ben: grabbing NVML stats: `nvidia-smi dmon` shows the GPU memory climb on the shard worker to 99% right before OOM. Suspect repeated oversized tensors due to TP resharding edge-case.

frank: collecting coredumps to /var/tmp/incidents/2045678901. Please keep them offline-only and encrypt before upload.

carla: can we toggle NCCL timeout shorter so hung collectives fail fast instead of starving other workloads?

ben: setting `NCCL_TIMEOUT=20` in runtime envs for affected pool. Patching helm values now.

alice: post-reroute numbers: error-rate down from 42% -> 6% in 3 minutes. Latency for fallback up ~15% but customers still getting responses.

gina: notifying impacted customers: "We've mitigated the issue by routing traffic to a fallback variant; investigating root cause. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Ticket owners updated.

dan: oncall handoff plan: I'll stay until stable metrics for 30m then hand to night SRE. If OOMs recur, escalate to runtime leads.

ella: recording action items: `A1` collect nvml & coredumps (ben/frank), `A2` patch NCCL/TORCH flags and test (ben), `A3` add safety request size cap on router (carla), `A4` postmortem (dan).

ben: quick repro attempt — running a stress harness with elongated context sizes replicates the OOM within 2 minutes when using TP shards + quantization path. Will add minimized repro and open an issue in infra/runtime repo.

carla: added a temporary router safeguard: max_tokens_per_request=8192 for this model route. Live config pushed.

alice: metric check at 03:47 UTC: stable error rate ~3%, nodes drained and restarted, core dumps uploaded to encrypted bucket (location provided to SRE).

frank: note: one node had nvlink flaps prior to OOMs, see kmsg: `NVLINK: link 1 down, retrying`. Could be hardware fragility + memory pressure.

dan: adding hardware vendor on a follow-up if we see reoccurrence. For now status -> MONITORING.

gina: customer comms updated with status: MONITORING and ETA for postmortem 24h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status changed to MONITORING by dan.

alice: handing off to night team in 30m. Leaving runbook note: if OOMs reappear, immediately reroute and scale fallback, collect nvml snapshot, and escalate to runtime-oncall.

ben: created runtime bug: infra/runtime#4321 with repro and links to dumps.

carla: thanks everyone. I'll follow up tomorrow with checklist for safety caps and routing failover tests. :thumbsup:

dan: closing notes: root cause hypothesis = unusual large-context requests hitting TP quantized path causing TF fragmentation and combined with nvlink instability triggered OOMs and NCCL timeouts. Postmortem in progress.

ella: handing to frank for overnight monitoring handoff.

frank: got it. I'll watch the dashboards and coordinate with hardware if needed.

alice: thanks all — great coordination.
